title: MATH GAOKAO - 2
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Roster Notation for a Finite Set
questions.learningObjective: Represent a set of positive integers less than \(6\) in roster notation.
questions.question: Which of the following is the roster form of the set of positive integers less than \(6\)?
questions.explanation: The positive integers less than \(6\) are \(1,2,3,4,5\). The number \(6\) is not less than \(6\), so it is excluded. Therefore the roster form is \(\{1,2,3,4,5\}\).
questions.hint: List positive integers and remember that “less than \(6\)” excludes \(6\) itself.

questions.concept: Conversion from Set-Builder Notation to Roster Notation
questions.learningObjective: Convert a set defined by an inequality over the integers into roster form.
questions.question: The set \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -1\le x<2\}\) in roster form is:
questions.explanation: The integers satisfying \(-1\le x<2\) are \(-1,0,1\). The endpoint \(2\) is not included because the inequality is \(x<2\). Hence \(A=\{-1,0,1\}\).
questions.hint: List the integers from \(-1\) up to but not including \(2\).

questions.concept: Interval Notation for a Real-Number Set
questions.learningObjective: Translate a set defined by a double inequality into interval notation.
questions.question: Which interval represents the set \(\{x\in\mathbb R\mid -3<x\le 1\}\)?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(-3<x\le 1\) means \(-3\) is excluded and \(1\) is included. In interval notation, an excluded endpoint uses a parenthesis and an included endpoint uses a bracket. Therefore the interval is \((-3,1]\).
questions.hint: Match strict inequalities to parentheses and non-strict inequalities to brackets.

questions.learningObjective: Express an interval as a set-builder notation using inequalities.
questions.question: Which set-builder notation describes the interval \([2,5)\)?
questions.explanation: The interval \([2,5)\) includes \(2\) and excludes \(5\). Therefore the corresponding inequality is \(2\le x<5\). So the set-builder notation is \(\{x\in\mathbb R\mid 2\le x<5\}\).
questions.hint: A square bracket means the endpoint is included, while a parenthesis means it is excluded.

questions.concept: Roster Form from an Inequality over the Integers
questions.learningObjective: Determine the integer elements satisfying a quadratic inequality and write them in roster form.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid x^2\le 4\}\). Which is the roster form of \(A\)?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(x^2\le 4\) is equivalent to \(-2\le x\le 2\). The integers in this interval are \(-2,-1,0,1,2\). Therefore \(A=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\).
questions.hint: Solve the inequality to find the range of \(x\), then list all integers in that range.

questions.concept: Interval Notation for a Union of Sets
questions.learningObjective: Write a set defined by a compound inequality as a union of intervals.
questions.question: Which interval notation represents \(\{x\in\mathbb R\mid x<-1 \text{ or } x\ge 3\}\)?
questions.explanation: The condition \(x<-1\) excludes \(-1\), so it corresponds to \((-\infty,-1)\). The condition \(x\ge 3\) includes \(3\), so it corresponds to \([3,\infty)\). Therefore the union is \((-\infty,-1)\cup[3,\infty)\).
questions.hint: Treat the two inequalities separately, then combine their interval forms with a union symbol.

questions.concept: Intersection of Sets Given in Set-Builder Notation
questions.learningObjective: Convert two sets from set-builder notation to roster form and find their intersection.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb N^+\mid x<4\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -1\le x\le 2\}\). Which is \(A\cap B\) in roster form?
questions.explanation: The set \(A\) consists of positive integers less than \(4\), so \(A=\{1,2,3\}\). The set \(B\) consists of integers from \(-1\) to \(2\), so \(B=\{-1,0,1,2\}\). The common elements are \(1\) and \(2\). Hence \(A\cap B=\{1,2\}\).
questions.hint: Write each set in roster form, then list only the elements that appear in both sets.

questions.concept: Interval Notation for a Quadratic Inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve a simple quadratic inequality and express the solution set in interval notation.
questions.question: The set \(\{x\in\mathbb R\mid x^2<9\}\) in interval notation is:
questions.explanation: The inequality \(x^2<9\) is equivalent to \(-3<x<3\). Since both endpoints are excluded, the interval notation is \((-3,3)\). The bracket notation \([-3,3]\) would incorrectly include \(-3\) and \(3\).
questions.hint: Rewrite the inequality as a double inequality before converting it to interval notation.

questions.concept: Cardinality of a Union of Sets Given in Set-Builder Notation
questions.learningObjective: Convert sets from set-builder notation to roster form and find the number of elements in their union.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid |x|<3\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb N^+\mid x\le 4\}\). How many elements are in \(A\cup B\)?
questions.explanation: The set \(A\) consists of integers with \(|x|<3\), so \(A=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\). The set \(B\) consists of positive integers at most \(4\), so \(B=\{1,2,3,4\}\). Their union is \(\{-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4\}\), which has \(7\) elements.
questions.hint: List both sets in roster form, combine all distinct elements, and then count them.

questions.learningObjective: Compare a real interval with an integer set and determine which is a subset of the other.
questions.question: Let \(A=\{x\in\mathbb R\mid x^2\le 4\}\) and \(B=\{x\in\mathbb Z\mid -3<x<3\}\). Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(x^2\le 4\) gives \(-2\le x\le 2\), so \(A=[-2,2]\). The set \(B\) consists of integers strictly between \(-3\) and \(3\), so \(B=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\). Every element of \(B\) lies in \(A\), so \(B\subseteq A\). However \(A\) contains non-integers such as \(0.5\), so \(A\nsubseteq B\). Therefore the true statement is \(B\subseteq A\).
questions.hint: Express \(A\) as an interval and list the integer elements of \(B\), then test the subset condition in both directions.
